pathway.title: Kinetik Holdings Inc. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Earnings and leverage are improving, but the improvement rests on an issuer-defined measure, so leverage sits between 3.70x and 4.57x rather than at one number. Debt over last-twelve-months adjusted EBITDA eased to 3.70x from 3.84x at 2025-12-31 and adjusted cash interest cover rose to 4.97x, while the 3.08x on reported EBITDA is flattered by a one-time gain of USD 415.41 million. No pro forma figure is established for the cash dividend paid on 2026-10-30, so period-end debt and leverage are stated as reported. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3

Payouts, not operations, are the main constraint: free cash flow does not cover distributions and borrowing fills the gap. Over the last twelve months free cash flow was USD 236.27 million against distributions of USD 521.18 million, a coverage of 0.45x, and carrying debt rose by USD 136.10 million in the nine months to 2026-09-30 after USD 288.72 million in 2025. The board declares distributions each quarter, so the gap is a policy choice that can be closed, which makes it the main lever as well as the main risk. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C4; calculation C5; calculation C6

Liquidity is adequate for the next year but is narrowing and has not been tested against covenants. It was USD 1,069.42 million at 2026-09-30, almost all of it undrawn revolver, down 12.57% from USD 1,223.15 million at 2025-12-31, and it covers the last-twelve-months payout shortfall of USD 284.92 million 3.75x. The receivables facility is fully drawn at USD 225.00 million and ends on 2027-03-30, and covenant levels are not printed, so headroom is not established. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 47; calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C4

Refinancing risk is concentrated in 2028, and the evidence on market access is dated. USD 2,200.00 million, or 55.70% of principal, falls due in 2028 across the term loan and the 2028 senior notes, with USD 1,525.00 million in 2030 and USD 225.00 million in 2027 through the receivables facility. The 2025 refinancing of the bank debt and an add-on to the 2028 senior notes priced above par show access then, but no ratings, quotes or covenant terms were supplied for now. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-K_2025-12-31_kntk-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation C9

Revenue visibility is weaker than recent earnings growth suggests, because volumes rest on a few producers and a thin contractual floor. Three customers produced 61.80% of 2025 revenue and committed revenue is about 1.05x one year of service revenue, while product sales are 80.15% of revenue and carried commodity hedge losses of between USD 49.90 million and USD 74.66 million in the nine months to 2026-09-30, depending on whether realized settlements are counted. Midstream Logistics adjusted EBITDA was 37.85% of its revenue in those nine months, up from 34.88% a year earlier but below the 43.47% of FY2023. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 31–32; 10-K_2025-12-31_kntk-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 146–147; calculation C11; calculation C15; calculation C17

A quarter of adjusted EBITDA reaches creditors only as partner distributions, which limits the weight the earnings can carry. Proportionate EBITDA of the equity-method pipelines was 26.23% of adjusted EBITDA in the nine months to 2026-09-30, down from 34.37% in FY2025 after the sale of the EPIC interest, and its cash arrives only if the operating partners distribute it. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 31–32; 10-K_2025-12-31_kntk-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 146; calculation C12

Interest cost is exposed to rates as hedges run off. USD 1,900.0 million of debt is floating and a 1.0% rate move would change annual interest expense by about USD 19.0 million before swaps, or 8.89% of last-twelve-months cash interest; the swaps on USD 1,000.0 million, fixed between 3.06% and 3.42%, end on 2026-12-31 for two contracts and on 2027-12-31 for five. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 52; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C13

Financial policy and governance are mixed rather than adverse. Two holders control a majority of voting shares and no priming or exchange transaction is disclosed, but payouts above free cash flow and share repurchases of USD 176.01 million in 2025 show equity returns taking priority over repayment of debt. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C5

cells.text: Integrated midstream energy company in the Permian Basin: natural gas gathering, compression, treating and processing; NGL stabilization and transportation; produced water gathering and disposal; crude oil gathering, stabilization, storage and transportation.
Midstream Logistics provides more than 99% of operating revenues. Pipeline Transportation holds all equity-method investments, which provide more than 88% of that segment's adjusted EBITDA.

Over 2.4 Bcf/d of cryogenic processing capacity at eight complexes in Texas and New Mexico. Management language: fourth largest natural gas processor in the Delaware Basin and in the Permian Basin by capacity.
55.5% of Permian Highway Pipeline (2.65 Bcf/d, operated by Kinder Morgan) and 33.0% of Breviloba, which owns the Shin Oak NGL pipeline (over 600 MBbl/d, operated by Enterprise).
Product sales 80.15%, service revenue 19.04% and other revenue 0.81% of USD 1,560.82 million revenue. Fee revenue booked inside cost of sales is not in service revenue.

Fee-based volumetric agreements, percent-of-proceeds, percent-of-products and product sales. Kinetik generally takes title to rich gas and plant products and sells them to downstream buyers, deducting its fees before remitting the balance.
Three customers each exceeded 10% of revenue in 2025 and together produced 61.80% of revenue; the largest produced 26.56%. Customers are not named.
USD 418.80 million at fixed price and volume at 2026-09-30, against USD 449.51 million at 2025-12-31.
2026 estimate of USD 450.0 million to USD 510.0 million, nearly 70% for New Mexico expansion; USD 347.77 million spent in the nine months to 2026-09-30.
The parent owned about 50% of Kinetik Holdings LP at 2026-09-30, equal to 49.55% of the combined Class A and Class C share count, and about 51% at 2026-11-03; Common Unit holders hold the rest.

runs.text: Liquidity is the first strength. Undrawn revolver capacity and cash of USD 1,069.42 million cover the last-twelve-months payout shortfall 3.75x, and the revolver runs to 2030, so on current figures and subject to covenants that are not printed, payouts can be funded without market access for several years. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 47; calculation C7; calculation C8

Debt service capacity is the second strength. Adjusted leverage eased to 3.70x and adjusted cash interest cover rose to 4.97x as Midstream Logistics adjusted EBITDA grew 26.90%, so interest is covered comfortably on the issuer-defined measure. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 31–32; calculation C1; calculation C3

Discretionary outflows are the third strength. The 2026 capital estimate is 3.71% to 15.04% below FY2025 spending, repurchases were paused through 2026-09-30 and distributions are declared quarterly by the board, which gives management levers to restore coverage. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kntk-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 73; 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 47; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C14

Scale and integration are the fourth strength. Over 2.4 Bcf/d of processing capacity with crude, water and pipeline assets in one basin supports volume capture on dedicated acreage. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_kntk-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 12

Reporting quality is the fifth strength. Audit opinions on the statements and on internal control are unqualified and segment disclosure is detailed, which supports monitoring, and no liability management transaction is disclosed. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kntk-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 90; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Payouts above free cash flow are the first weakness. Distributions of USD 521.18 million against free cash flow of USD 236.27 million over the last twelve months are covered 0.45x, so debt rises unless EBITDA outgrows it, which raises the size of the 2028 refinancing. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C4; calculation C6

Maturity concentration in 2028 is the second weakness. USD 2,200.00 million, or 55.70% of principal, falls due in 2028, and the receivables facility ends on 2027-03-30, so refinancing must be completed within two years while ratings and covenant headroom are not shown. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation C9

Customer concentration with a thin contractual floor is the third weakness. Three customers produced 61.80% of 2025 revenue and committed revenue is about 1.05x one year of service revenue, so a cut by one producer would reach EBITDA before costs fall. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C15

Earnings quality is the fourth weakness. Leverage ranges from 3.70x to 4.57x depending on the one-time gain, and 26.23% of adjusted EBITDA is partner-operated pipeline earnings that arrive as distributions, so the cleanest cash earnings are smaller than the headline. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C2; calculation C12

Commodity, single-basin and rate exposure is the fifth weakness. Product sales are 80.15% of revenue, all assets sit in the Permian Basin and USD 1,900.0 million of debt is floating with swaps ending by 2027-12-31, so price and rate moves reach cash flow quickly. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 52; calculation C13

cells.text: Kinetik Holdings Inc., a Delaware corporation formerly named Altus Midstream Company.
Class A common stock listed as KNTK on the New York Stock Exchange and NYSE Texas.
United States; Permian Basin in Texas and New Mexico.
Midstream oil and gas: gathering, processing, treating and pipeline transportation.
Corporate office in Houston, Texas; operational headquarters in Midland, Texas.
More than 500 at 2025-12-31, none covered by collective bargaining agreements.
KPMG LLP: opinion on the FY2025 statements is unmodified and the report on internal control is unqualified; the critical audit matter is the evaluation of impairment indicators for long-lived assets.

Class A common stock 80,459,324 shares and Class C common stock 81,936,866 shares, the latter equal in number to Common Units of Kinetik Holdings LP, carried as redeemable noncontrolling interest of USD 4,207.024 million.

Kinetik Holdings LP borrows and issues notes; the parent guarantees the term loan, the revolver and the 2030 notes, and the FY2024 annual report also states that it guarantees the 2028 notes, which the FY2025 annual report does not restate.
Nine months to 2026-09-30: revenue USD 1,560.82 million; issuer-defined adjusted EBITDA USD 810.13 million.

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: Kinetik has no pending acquisition, merger or sponsor transaction in the supplied filings; its history is a series of completed purchases and sales. The Durango Acquisition closed on 2024-06-24 at an adjusted purchase price of about USD 785.67 million, made up of cash of USD 357.97 million, Common Units of USD 148.20 million, deferred Class C consideration of USD 275.00 million and contingent consideration of USD 4.50 million. The Barilla Draw Acquisition closed on 2025-01-14 for USD 175.50 million in cash. Kinetik sold its 16% interest in GCX on 2024-06-04 for an adjusted price of USD 524.40 million, and sold its 27.5% interest in EPIC on 2025-10-31 for USD 504.20 million upfront plus a possible earnout of about USD 96.00 million. Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_kntk-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 102; 10-K_2025-12-31_kntk-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 119; 10-K_2025-12-31_kntk-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; 10-K_2025-12-31_kntk-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 123; calculation K21; calculation K25

New debt in the period was raised at the Partnership. USD 250.00 million of additional 6.625% sustainability-linked senior notes due 2028 were placed on 2025-03-14 at 101.25% of par. On 2025-05-30 a USD 1.15 billion term loan maturing in 2028 and a USD 1.60 billion revolving facility maturing in 2030 replaced the 2022 facilities. The receivables facility was amended on 2025-04-01 to a limit of USD 250.00 million, then cut to USD 225.00 million with its sustainability-linked pricing removed and extended to 2027-03-30 on 2026-03-31, and on 2026-10-30 Kinetik Receivables requested an increase of USD 50.00 million to USD 275.00 million. In the nine months to 2026-09-30 there were no term borrowings, only revolver and receivables facility draws. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kntk-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation K19

Two contingent amounts could change cash flows. The Kings Landing earnout of up to USD 75.00 million is payable to the Durango seller and can be reduced for actual project costs, and the EPIC earnout of about USD 96.00 million is receivable by Kinetik if projects that meet capacity expansion criteria are approved. The final amount and timing of neither is stated. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kntk-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 119; 10-K_2025-12-31_kntk-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; 10-K_2025-12-31_kntk-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 123

fields.value: Financial foundation for Kinetik Holdings Inc. (issuer id kntk-1692787) as of 2026-11-18 under the credit snapshot pathway, on the filed statements through the quarter ended 2026-09-30. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Debt at carrying value rose from USD 3,792.920m at 2025-12-31 to USD 3,929.022m at 2026-09-30, while issuer-adjusted last-twelve-month EBITDA rose from USD 987.704m to USD 1,062.248m, so adjusted leverage eased from 3.84x to 3.70x. The ease depends on the issuer-defined measure, which counts the proportionate EBITDA of pipelines that pay the company only through distributions, so lenders carry that structural subordination.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The reported-EBITDA ratio of 3.08x is not the safer reading. It includes a gain of USD 415.409m on the sale of the EPIC pipeline interest recognized in the fourth quarter of 2025, and equity earnings that arrive as cash only through distributions. Without the gain the ratio is 4.57x, which brackets the credit between 3.70x and 4.57x depending on how the pipeline earnings are valued. Cash interest cover on the adjusted measure was 4.97x, up from 4.57x in FY2025, because cash interest paid was little changed while EBITDA rose.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Nine-month 2026 operating cash flow of USD 614.387m less capital expenditure of USD 347.771m left free cash flow of USD 266.616m, against distributions of USD 394.886m to Class A shareholders and Class C unitholders, a shortfall of USD 128.270m. The shortfall was met by net borrowing on the revolver and the receivables facility, so every dollar of distribution above free cash flow adds to debt and the payout is a call on lenders rather than on retained cash. In FY2025 distributions of USD 500.052m also exceeded free cash flow of USD 74.449m, and the gap was covered only by USD 504.184m of sale proceeds from the EPIC interest, which do not recur.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-K_2025-12-31_kntk-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 96–97; calculation K05; calculation K12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: About a third of operating cash flow is distributions from the equity-method pipelines (USD 203.426m of USD 614.387m in nine months 2026), so cash flow quality depends on two pipelines whose statements are not supplied in full. Working capital absorbed cash in the period through a USD 115.391m increase in receivables, offset by a USD 169.441m rise in accrued liabilities driven by product purchases and accrued interest, so the strong operating cash flow partly reflects timing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity at 2026-09-30 was USD 1,069.424m, made of USD 7.024m of cash and USD 1,062.400m of undrawn revolver capacity after USD 12.600m of letters of credit, down from USD 1,223.151m at 2025-12-31. The receivables facility is fully drawn at USD 225.000m and its scheduled termination of 2027-03-30 falls within twelve months of the balance sheet date, while commitments were raised by USD 50.0 million on 2026-10-30, an event kept out of period figures.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Principal of USD 3,950.000m matures as USD 225.000m in 2027, USD 2,200.000m in 2028 (the term loan and the 2028 Notes) and USD 1,525.000m in 2030 (the 2030 Notes and the revolver), so more than half of principal falls due in a single year with no scheduled amortization before then. The 2028 maturities are therefore the refinancing question for creditors, and the undrawn revolver, which matures in 2030, is the committed liquidity that spans them.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The statements reconcile: assets equal liabilities plus temporary equity plus equity at every balance sheet date, the three activity totals add to the net change in cash, opening cash plus the change equals closing cash, and the quarterly revenues add to the year-to-date totals in both years. Four definition choices move the credit view and are logged: derived reported EBITDA against issuer-adjusted EBITDA, one-time sale gains, equity-method earnings against proportionate EBITDA, and the netting of gas service revenues in cost of sales.

This restricts structural priority and recovery work. Severity High. Action: obtain the indentures, the credit agreements and the receivables purchase agreement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business & governance for Kinetik Holdings Inc. (issuer id kntk-1692787) as of 2026-11-18 under the credit snapshot pathway, from the five supplied filings through the quarter ended 2026-09-30. Scope is the business and operating model, ownership and control, transaction and event history, governance, sponsor behavior and capital allocation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Kinetik is a concentrated Permian midstream business whose creditors rely on a few producers and on equity payouts that currently exceed free cash flow, so sponsor and governance risk is medium, not low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kntk-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2025-12-31_kntk-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-K_2025-12-31_kntk-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 104; calculation K1; calculation K15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Three customers produced 61.80% of 2025 revenue, and contractually committed revenue of USD 418.80 million is about 1.05x one year of service revenue, so volumes depend on producer drilling more than on contracts. In the nine months to 2026-09-30, cash distributions of USD 394.89 million exceeded free cash flow of USD 266.62 million, and net borrowing of USD 131.80 million covered the gap.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kntk-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 104; 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8; calculation K1; calculation K10; calculation K15; calculation K19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue concentration is high and contractual protection is thin, so creditor cash flow follows a few producers' drilling decisions. Three customers each exceeded 10% of revenue and together produced 61.80% of 2025 revenue, against 71.27% in 2024 and 57.04% in 2023, and the largest alone produced 26.56%. Contractually committed revenue at fixed price and volume is USD 418.80 million at 2026-09-30, about 1.05x one year of last-twelve-months service revenue of USD 398.82 million, and minimum volume deficiency payments were only USD 4.6 million in the nine months. The customers are not named, so their credit quality is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kntk-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 104; 10-K_2024-12-31_kntk-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 111; 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation K1; calculation K2; calculation K3; calculation K4; calculation K10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reported service revenue understates the fee base, because part of the fee revenue is now booked inside cost of sales, so the apparent move toward commodity-linked revenue is overstated. In the nine months to 2026-09-30 service revenue fell 13.57% and product revenue rose 27.43%, but fee revenue booked inside cost of sales rose USD 89.90 million; counting it, fee revenue grew 7.61%. Product sales are still 80.15% of revenue and carry commodity price and hedging exposure, with hedging losses of USD 49.90 million against a gain of USD 13.40 million a year earlier.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 40; calculation K7; calculation K8; calculation K9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A quarter of adjusted EBITDA comes from pipelines that Kinetik owns only in part and does not operate, so that cash reaches creditors as distributions rather than under Kinetik's control. Proportionate EBITDA of the equity-method pipelines was 26.23% of adjusted EBITDA in the nine months to 2026-09-30, down from 35.80% a year earlier after the 2025 sale of the EPIC interest, while the Midstream Logistics segment grew its adjusted EBITDA 26.90% and the Pipeline Transportation segment's fell 16.29%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 30–32; 10-K_2025-12-31_kntk-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; 10-K_2025-12-31_kntk-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation K12; calculation K13; calculation K14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Control rests with two large holders, and no conduct adverse to creditors is documented, which supports a medium governance risk rather than a high one. Entities controlled by Blackstone and I Squared Capital held a majority of the voting shares when the 2025 annual report was filed, and each may designate directors while it holds at least 10% of the common stock; their current holdings and any fees are not stated. The only related-party flow disclosed is pipeline capacity and demand fees of USD 28.55 million in 2025, after the former related party Apache sold its last shares by 2024-03-18.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kntk-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2025-12-31_kntk-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-K_2025-12-31_kntk-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 144; calculation K23

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Equity payouts have run ahead of free cash flow and borrowing or asset sales have covered the difference, which is the main way ownership decisions reach creditors. In the nine months to 2026-09-30, cash distributions were USD 394.89 million against free cash flow of USD 266.62 million, so coverage was 0.68x, up from 0.28x a year earlier, and net borrowing under the revolver and the receivables facility was USD 131.80 million. In 2025, distributions and share repurchases of USD 676.06 million exceeded free cash flow of USD 74.45 million, alongside USD 504.18 million of proceeds from selling the EPIC interest; no shares were repurchased in the nine months to 2026-09-30.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-K_2025-12-31_kntk-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 96–97; calculation K15; calculation K16; calculation K17; calculation K19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Acquisitions have been funded partly with units, and unit holders can redeem into Class A shares at no cash cost to the Partnership, so economic ownership is moving from units into Class A shares without new debt. About 45.56% of the USD 785.67 million Durango price was cash and 53.87% was Common Units and deferred Class C shares, and redemptions raised the parent's share of Class A and Class C shares from 39.64% at 2025-12-31 to 49.55% at 2026-09-30; the identities of the redeeming holders are not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_kntk-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 102; 10-K_2024-12-31_kntk-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 104; 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; calculation K20; calculation K21

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A contract dispute with Energy Transfer is partly settled and partly open, so event risk around the NGL purchase agreements remains until the court rules. In October 2026 the parties confirmed that the term of one NGL purchase agreement ends on 2026-12-31, while two lawsuits over two long-term NGL purchase agreements remained pending after a bench trial in March and April 2026; accrued reserves are immaterial, and the filing does not say whether the settlement ends the lawsuits or what the earnings effect of the term ending is.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a medium reading is operating and financial improvement. Adjusted EBITDA of the Midstream Logistics segment rose 26.90% in the nine months to 2026-09-30, free cash flow rose to USD 266.62 million from USD 104.80 million a year earlier, and no shares were repurchased in the nine months to 2026-09-30. Kinetik typically takes title to the gas and products it processes and sells them to downstream buyers it describes as large investment grade entities, deducting its fees before remitting the balance, which on its account limits credit risk from producers. Unit redemptions cost no cash, and the filings disclose no priming, drop-down, exchange or sponsor fee transactions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 31–32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-K_2025-12-31_kntk-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 104; calculation K14; calculation K15; calculation K16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would move to low if distributions were covered in full by free cash flow for several consecutive quarters, if sponsor holdings and any fees were disclosed with no leakage, and if committed revenue grew. It would move to high if repurchases resumed with borrowed money, if a sponsor or related-party payment appeared, if one of the three largest customers cut volumes, if the court ruled against Kinetik on the NGL agreements, or if the debt documents showed room to move assets away from creditors.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Kinetik has no pending acquisition, merger or sponsor transaction in the supplied filings; its history is a series of completed purchases and sales. The Durango Acquisition closed on 2024-06-24 at an adjusted purchase price of about USD 785.67 million, made up of cash of USD 357.97 million, Common Units of USD 148.20 million, deferred Class C consideration of USD 275.00 million and contingent consideration of USD 4.50 million. The Barilla Draw Acquisition closed on 2025-01-14 for USD 175.50 million in cash. Kinetik sold its 16% interest in GCX on 2024-06-04 for an adjusted price of USD 524.40 million, and sold its 27.5% interest in EPIC on 2025-10-31 for USD 504.20 million upfront plus a possible earnout of about USD 96.00 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: New debt in the period was raised at the Partnership. USD 250.00 million of additional 6.625% sustainability-linked senior notes due 2028 were placed on 2025-03-14 at 101.25% of par. On 2025-05-30 a USD 1.15 billion term loan maturing in 2028 and a USD 1.60 billion revolving facility maturing in 2030 replaced the 2022 facilities. The receivables facility was amended on 2025-04-01 to a limit of USD 250.00 million, then cut to USD 225.00 million with its sustainability-linked pricing removed and extended to 2027-03-30 on 2026-03-31, and on 2026-10-30 Kinetik Receivables requested an increase of USD 50.00 million to USD 275.00 million. In the nine months to 2026-09-30 there were no term borrowings, only revolver and receivables facility draws.

fields.value: Two contingent amounts could change cash flows. The Kings Landing earnout of up to USD 75.00 million is payable to the Durango seller and can be reduced for actual project costs, and the EPIC earnout of about USD 96.00 million is receivable by Kinetik if projects that meet capacity expansion criteria are approved. The final amount and timing of neither is stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit for Kinetik Holdings Inc. (issuer id kntk-1692787) as of 2026-11-18 under the credit snapshot pathway, from the filings through the quarter ended 2026-09-30 and the supplied analyses of source readiness, the financial foundation and the business. Scope is the overall fundamental credit view, its strongest support and weakest points, the primary downside path and what to monitor.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Kinetik's fundamental credit is adequate but constrained: earnings are growing, yet payouts above free cash flow keep adding debt ahead of USD 2,200.00 million of 2028 maturities, so creditors rely on the revolver and on the board holding distributions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation C4; calculation C9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Debt at carrying value of USD 3,929.02 million is 3.70x last-twelve-months adjusted EBITDA but 4.57x without a one-time sale gain, and free cash flow covered only 0.45x of distributions over the last twelve months. Liquidity of USD 1,069.42 million covers that shortfall 3.75x, so the first break would come in leverage and refinancing rather than in cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C4; calculation C7; calculation C8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings and leverage are improving, but the improvement rests on an issuer-defined measure, so leverage sits between 3.70x and 4.57x rather than at one number. Debt over last-twelve-months adjusted EBITDA eased to 3.70x from 3.84x at 2025-12-31 and adjusted cash interest cover rose to 4.97x, while the 3.08x on reported EBITDA is flattered by a one-time gain of USD 415.41 million. No pro forma figure is established for the cash dividend paid on 2026-10-30, so period-end debt and leverage are stated as reported.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Payouts, not operations, are the main constraint: free cash flow does not cover distributions and borrowing fills the gap. Over the last twelve months free cash flow was USD 236.27 million against distributions of USD 521.18 million, a coverage of 0.45x, and carrying debt rose by USD 136.10 million in the nine months to 2026-09-30 after USD 288.72 million in 2025. The board declares distributions each quarter, so the gap is a policy choice that can be closed, which makes it the main lever as well as the main risk.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C4; calculation C5; calculation C6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is adequate for the next year but is narrowing and has not been tested against covenants. It was USD 1,069.42 million at 2026-09-30, almost all of it undrawn revolver, down 12.57% from USD 1,223.15 million at 2025-12-31, and it covers the last-twelve-months payout shortfall of USD 284.92 million 3.75x. The receivables facility is fully drawn at USD 225.00 million and ends on 2027-03-30, and covenant levels are not printed, so headroom is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 47; calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Refinancing risk is concentrated in 2028, and the evidence on market access is dated. USD 2,200.00 million, or 55.70% of principal, falls due in 2028 across the term loan and the 2028 senior notes, with USD 1,525.00 million in 2030 and USD 225.00 million in 2027 through the receivables facility. The 2025 refinancing of the bank debt and an add-on to the 2028 senior notes priced above par show access then, but no ratings, quotes or covenant terms were supplied for now.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-K_2025-12-31_kntk-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation C9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue visibility is weaker than recent earnings growth suggests, because volumes rest on a few producers and a thin contractual floor. Three customers produced 61.80% of 2025 revenue and committed revenue is about 1.05x one year of service revenue, while product sales are 80.15% of revenue and carried commodity hedge losses of between USD 49.90 million and USD 74.66 million in the nine months to 2026-09-30, depending on whether realized settlements are counted. Midstream Logistics adjusted EBITDA was 37.85% of its revenue in those nine months, up from 34.88% a year earlier but below the 43.47% of FY2023.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 31–32; 10-K_2025-12-31_kntk-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 146–147; calculation C11; calculation C15; calculation C17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A quarter of adjusted EBITDA reaches creditors only as partner distributions, which limits the weight the earnings can carry. Proportionate EBITDA of the equity-method pipelines was 26.23% of adjusted EBITDA in the nine months to 2026-09-30, down from 34.37% in FY2025 after the sale of the EPIC interest, and its cash arrives only if the operating partners distribute it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 31–32; 10-K_2025-12-31_kntk-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 146; calculation C12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Interest cost is exposed to rates as hedges run off. USD 1,900.0 million of debt is floating and a 1.0% rate move would change annual interest expense by about USD 19.0 million before swaps, or 8.89% of last-twelve-months cash interest; the swaps on USD 1,000.0 million, fixed between 3.06% and 3.42%, end on 2026-12-31 for two contracts and on 2027-12-31 for five.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 52; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy and governance are mixed rather than adverse. Two holders control a majority of voting shares and no priming or exchange transaction is disclosed, but payouts above free cash flow and share repurchases of USD 176.01 million in 2025 show equity returns taking priority over repayment of debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence for a better view is that cash generation is improving and management says it is sufficient. Free cash flow rose to USD 266.62 million in the nine months to 2026-09-30 from USD 104.80 million a year earlier, Midstream Logistics adjusted EBITDA grew 26.90%, adjusted leverage eased and the 2026 capital estimate is 3.71% to 15.04% below FY2025 spending. Management states that cash from operations, pipeline distributions and remaining borrowing capacity will exceed capital expenditure and the planned quarterly dividend over the next 12 months; that statement counts borrowing capacity as a source, so it is consistent with payouts funded by debt rather than a contradiction of it. Kinetik also takes title to products and sells to downstream buyers it describes as large investment grade entities, which limits credit risk from producers.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-K_2025-12-31_kntk-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 73; 10-K_2025-12-31_kntk-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 104; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C5; calculation C11; calculation C14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would improve if free cash flow covered distributions in full for several consecutive quarters, if the board reset the payout, or if the gap between adjusted and ex-gain leverage narrowed as pipeline earnings proved durable. It would worsen if one of the three largest customers cut volumes, if payouts continued while free cash flow fell, if the receivables facility were not extended before 2027-03-30, or if the 2028 refinancing had to be priced at higher leverage than today.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Covenant levels, ratings and market prices were not supplied, so the liquidity and refinancing conclusions rest on facility size, maturity and the 2025 refinancing alone and would weaken if a covenant binds before the revolver is exhausted.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No peer or sector data were supplied, so the adequate business profile is a judgement on Kinetik's own facts and is not ranked against other leveraged midstream issuers.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The split of capital spending between maintenance and growth and the split of costs into fixed and variable are not stated, so the cost and capex flexibility view rests on the 2026 estimate and past spending and would fall if maintenance is a large share.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The dividend paid on 2026-10-30 has no stated effect on period-end cash, debt or leverage, and the USD 50.0 million increase in receivables facility commitments requested on that date is outside the balance sheet figures, so liquidity and leverage after those events are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The downside sensitivities cut last-twelve-months adjusted EBITDA by fixed percentages with debt and cash interest held flat, so they show scale rather than forecast and ignore hedges, management actions and covenant tests.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is the first strength. Undrawn revolver capacity and cash of USD 1,069.42 million cover the last-twelve-months payout shortfall 3.75x, and the revolver runs to 2030, so on current figures and subject to covenants that are not printed, payouts can be funded without market access for several years.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 47; calculation C7; calculation C8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Debt service capacity is the second strength. Adjusted leverage eased to 3.70x and adjusted cash interest cover rose to 4.97x as Midstream Logistics adjusted EBITDA grew 26.90%, so interest is covered comfortably on the issuer-defined measure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 31–32; calculation C1; calculation C3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Discretionary outflows are the third strength. The 2026 capital estimate is 3.71% to 15.04% below FY2025 spending, repurchases were paused through 2026-09-30 and distributions are declared quarterly by the board, which gives management levers to restore coverage.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kntk-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 73; 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 47; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scale and integration are the fourth strength. Over 2.4 Bcf/d of processing capacity with crude, water and pipeline assets in one basin supports volume capture on dedicated acreage.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reporting quality is the fifth strength. Audit opinions on the statements and on internal control are unqualified and segment disclosure is detailed, which supports monitoring, and no liability management transaction is disclosed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Payouts above free cash flow are the first weakness. Distributions of USD 521.18 million against free cash flow of USD 236.27 million over the last twelve months are covered 0.45x, so debt rises unless EBITDA outgrows it, which raises the size of the 2028 refinancing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C4; calculation C6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Maturity concentration in 2028 is the second weakness. USD 2,200.00 million, or 55.70% of principal, falls due in 2028, and the receivables facility ends on 2027-03-30, so refinancing must be completed within two years while ratings and covenant headroom are not shown.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation C9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Customer concentration with a thin contractual floor is the third weakness. Three customers produced 61.80% of 2025 revenue and committed revenue is about 1.05x one year of service revenue, so a cut by one producer would reach EBITDA before costs fall.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings quality is the fourth weakness. Leverage ranges from 3.70x to 4.57x depending on the one-time gain, and 26.23% of adjusted EBITDA is partner-operated pipeline earnings that arrive as distributions, so the cleanest cash earnings are smaller than the headline.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C2; calculation C12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Commodity, single-basin and rate exposure is the fifth weakness. Product sales are 80.15% of revenue, all assets sit in the Permian Basin and USD 1,900.0 million of debt is floating with swaps ending by 2027-12-31, so price and rate moves reach cash flow quickly.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 52; calculation C13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Kinetik is a Permian Basin midstream operator that gathers, compresses, treats and processes natural gas, stabilizes and transports NGLs, gathers and disposes of produced water, and gathers and stores crude, with over 2.4 Bcf/d of processing capacity and minority stakes in two long-term contracted pipelines. For creditors the model gives fee-based cash flow tied to producers' drilling on dedicated acreage plus commodity exposure through product sales, so cash-flow visibility is moderate and depends on volumes rather than on long take-or-pay contracts.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The parent is a holding company that owns about 50% of Kinetik Holdings LP, the borrower and note issuer, and guarantees the term loan, the revolver and the 2030 senior notes, so creditor claims sit at the Partnership while only consolidated statements are supplied. Entities controlled by Blackstone and I Squared Capital held a majority of the voting shares when the 2025 annual report was filed, and the Business & governance view of sponsor and governance risk is medium because no adverse conduct is documented while payouts exceed free cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue durability is moderate. The volume driver is producers' completion activity on dedicated acreage, which the company says depends on its customers' development and declines naturally from existing wells, and the price driver is fee rates plus, for product sales, NGL, condensate and gas prices. Committed revenue at fixed price and volume is USD 418.80 million, about 1.05x one year of service revenue, and minimum volume deficiency payments were USD 4.6 million in the nine months to 2026-09-30. Three customers produced 61.80% of 2025 revenue, and the contracts allow customers to suspend, reduce or terminate obligations after non-performance or force majeure events. Revenue is therefore recurring in form but concentrated and cyclical with producer activity, and a drilling slowdown would cut volumes before fees reset, which reaches EBITDA and then payout coverage.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kntk-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-12-31_kntk-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 27–28; 10-K_2025-12-31_kntk-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margin resilience is average. Cost of sales moves with product volumes and prices, and operating expenses of USD 213.86 million in the nine months to 2026-09-30, 3% higher, sit almost entirely in Midstream Logistics; the split between fixed and variable cost is not stated. Midstream Logistics adjusted EBITDA was 43.47% of segment revenue in FY2023, 41.73% in FY2024 and 36.23% in FY2025 as product sales raised revenue, then 37.85% in the nine months to 2026-09-30 against 34.88% a year earlier. Margin on revenue therefore does not rise with revenue, and the cost base cannot be tested against volume declines from the filings, so operating leverage is a risk that is assumed rather than measured.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-K_2025-12-31_kntk-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 146–147; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash conversion is adequate but absorbed by payouts. Operating cash flow was 75.84% of adjusted EBITDA in the nine months to 2026-09-30, capital expenditure was USD 347.77 million and free cash flow USD 266.62 million, yet last-twelve-months free cash flow of USD 236.27 million left a USD 284.92 million shortfall after distributions. The 2026 capital estimate of USD 450.0 million to USD 510.0 million, nearly 70% for New Mexico expansion, is 3.71% to 15.04% below FY2025, and the ECCC pipeline entered service in June 2026 and Kings Landing in September 2025, so part of the remaining growth spending is discretionary; the maintenance share is not stated. Working capital moved cash both ways, with receivables up USD 115.39 million and accrued liabilities up USD 169.44 million, so single-period cash flow is flattered by timing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_kntk-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 73; 10-K_2025-12-31_kntk-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 119; 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; calculation C4; calculation C14; calculation C16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is intense. The company faces intense competition for gas and NGL volumes from integrated producers, pipelines and other midstream firms, based on location, reputation and pricing, so fees can be pressured when contracts roll and volumes can be lost where acreage is not dedicated; this moderates fee durability.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Threat of new entrants is moderate. Competitors may expand or build gathering systems and customers may build their own, which would cut volumes on the affected acreage; Kinetik's existing processing capacity and dedicated acreage slow but do not prevent this.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Substitutes are a long-term rather than a near-term threat. Other forms of energy compete with hydrocarbons, which would reduce producer activity over time, but no near-term effect on the credit is shown in the filings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Buyer power is high. Producers can suspend, reduce or terminate obligations after non-performance or force majeure, and three customers account for most revenue, so contract terms give creditors limited protection against a customer's decision to move volumes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Supplier power is moderate. Kinetik relies on third-party pipelines for residue gas and NGL outlets and faces equipment and skilled-labor shortages; a dispute with Energy Transfer over long-term NGL purchase agreements shows how a counterparty on the NGL chain can affect margin, although its effect is not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_kntk-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-12-31_kntk-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_kntk-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-12-31_kntk-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Economic and regulatory factors are material; social and technological factors are not a primary credit driver on the filings. Commodity prices and interest rates reach cash flow through product sales, hedge results and USD 1,900.0 million of floating debt. Regulation of hydraulic fracturing and of produced-water disposal tied to induced seismic activity could slow producers or limit water volumes, and trade policy and tariffs raise cost and activity risk; none is quantified in the filings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths are the liquidity cushion against the payout shortfall, improving adjusted leverage and cash interest cover, integrated gathering and processing scale with dedicated acreage, and discretionary capital spending. Weaknesses are payouts above free cash flow, the 2028 maturity concentration, customer concentration with a thin contractual floor, and earnings that partly arrive as partner distributions. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are the completed ECCC and Kings Landing projects adding volumes, a possible earnout of about USD 96.0 million from the EPIC sale, and a lower payout restoring coverage. Threats that could weaken it are a producer slowdown, lower NGL and condensate prices, rising rates as swaps end, and an adverse ruling in the Energy Transfer lawsuits.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-09-30_kntk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-K_2025-12-31_kntk-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main supports are liquidity of USD 1,069.42 million against a payout shortfall of USD 284.92 million a year, adjusted leverage easing to 3.70x with cash interest cover of 4.97x, a revolver maturing in 2030 and discretionary capital spending. The main constraints are distributions that exceed free cash flow, a leverage reading that moves to 4.57x without the one-time gain, 55.70% of principal due in 2028 and a receivables facility due on 2027-03-30. The trend is better on earnings and worse on debt: segment EBITDA is rising while carrying debt rose by USD 136.10 million in nine months. The missing datapoints that would settle the view are covenant levels, ratings, peer leverage and the maintenance share of capital spending.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C6; calculation C7; calculation C9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next 12 to 24 months the tailwinds are the ECCC and Kings Landing capacity now in service, interest expense that fell 7% in the nine months to 2026-09-30 on lower debt balances and swap gains, a lower 2026 capital estimate and an agreed end date for one NGL purchase agreement. The headwinds are the end of that agreement on 2026-12-31 with an earnings effect that is not stated, two interest rate swaps ending on 2026-12-31 and five on 2027-12-31, the receivables facility due on 2027-03-30 and a payout that exceeds free cash flow. Over three to five years the 2028 maturities, natural decline in producer wells and the need to keep volumes on dedicated acreage dominate; none of this is quantified by management guidance, because the filings state none.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The initiating condition is a slowdown in Delaware Basin completions as NGL and condensate prices weaken, which the company lists among its principal risks because volumes depend on customers' drilling on dedicated acreage. The first operational break is lower gathered and processed volumes; committed revenue of USD 418.80 million is only about 1.05x one year of service revenue, so it cushions little, and commodity swaps cover stated notional volumes only for the next 1 to 27 months with the hedged share of production not stated, so protection at lower prices is not established. Financial transmission runs through adjusted EBITDA and through the USD 203.43 million of pipeline distributions received in nine months, which fall if partner-operated volumes fall; a 10% fall in last-twelve-months adjusted EBITDA gives 4.11x leverage and 4.47x cover, and a 20% fall gives 4.62x and 3.98x, with debt and cash interest held flat. Distributions of USD 521.18 million continue until the board acts, so the payout shortfall grows beyond USD 284.92 million and is met from the revolver; liquidity of USD 1,069.42 million covers the current shortfall 3.75x, so a liquidity crisis is not indicated within the next year on these figures, subject to covenants that are not printed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Kinetik presents an adequate business profile supported by integrated Permian gathering and processing scale, growing segment earnings and adjusted cash interest cover of 4.97x, but credit quality is constrained by payouts above free cash flow, customer concentration and the 2028 maturities. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because earnings are rising and capital spending is discretionary, yet last-twelve-months free cash flow covers only 0.45x of distributions. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on whether the board holds distributions, on covenant headroom and on the Partnership's rating, none of which is in the supplied filings. The primary downside path is producer activity or prices falling while payouts continue. Further analysis would require the credit agreements and indentures, ratings, market prices, peer leverage and customer terms; the business profile against typical leveraged midstream issuers is not established.
